one_line: Passive web-security scanning with explicit human authorization and shared agent state.
what_it_does: Scans authorized domains for common passive security issues, explains findings, proposes fixes, and logs human/agent actions.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools and human approval boundaries make the agent central to a stateful security workflow that is materially safer and more reliable than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and description specify seven document.modelContext tools.
Shared audit log records human and agent actions.
Human authorization is required before domain scanning and state-changing actions are excluded.
execution_rationale: The frame sheet shows a coherent landing, authorization, scan, and scored-results flow, though individual checks and end-to-end verification are not legible.
execution_evidence: Viewed frame sheet shows domain input, authorization messaging, scanner controls, results card, and 100/100 score claim.
Demo is marked alive and a public repository is present.
impact_rationale: Website owners have a concrete, underserved need for understandable passive security checks; the safety framing directly addresses authorization risk.
impact_evidence: Description names HTTPS, HSTS, CSP, cookie flags, and exposed .env as practical checks.
Plain-language severity explanations and copy-paste fixes target non-security owners.
creativity_rationale: Human-in-the-loop authorization as a product boundary is a thoughtful synthesis of agent automation and security ethics.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly separates agent-run passive work from human authorization.
Shared auditability is integrated into the concept.
usability_note: Clear guided flow and plain-language fixes; scan authorization adds useful friction.
red_flags: No transcript and small frame text limits verification of tool invocation and fix verification.
standouts: Strong safety boundary between passive scanning and human authorization.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-centered security workflow with credible value and visible product flow.

one_line: Evidence-governed product-truth reconciliation for enterprise claims.
what_it_does: Checks claims across marketing, runtime, contract, and repository evidence; exposes provenance and stages local copy changes without falsely calling them production fixes.
leverage_rationale: The structured claim IDs, authority rules, provenance, and claim ceiling encode a domain contract that a general UI-driving agent would struggle to infer reliably.
leverage_evidence: Deterministic BLOCK/REVIEW/ALIGNED/NOT_EVALUATED classifications.
Tools return explicit claim IDs, inputs, side-effect annotations, and evidence authority.
Human and agent focus the same claim and share staged state.
execution_rationale: The described workflow is unusually coherent and bounded, with explicit non-issuing staged state; frame sheets provide product-motion evidence but no transcript.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets submitted for the product workflow.
Description covers inspect, trace, focus, stage, rerun, and terminal staged status.
Public repository and alive demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Enterprise teams have a real governance problem when product claims drift across surfaces; authoritative reconciliation can prevent sales and trust failures.
impact_evidence: Targets marketing/pricing/docs/trust/contract/runtime drift.
Identifies blocking claims for an enterprise sales gate and preserves production authority.
creativity_rationale: Treating product truth as a callable, authority-aware evidence graph with a strict claim ceiling is a novel and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Sandbox changes deliberately cannot be labeled fixed.
Authority and provenance are first-class visible concepts.
usability_note: Structured verdicts and claim focus should reduce ambiguity, though the domain model is sophisticated.
red_flags: Synthetic evidence graph may not demonstrate production deployment breadth.
standouts: Excellent separation of evidence authority, staging, and production verification.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-leverage agent-native governance workflow with strong coherence.

leverage_rationale: Multi-step constraint handling and replanning benefit from structured tools, though a capable general agent could achieve much of this through travel UIs.
leverage_evidence: Tools cover search, itinerary creation, shortlists, budgets, and replanning.

usability_note: Shared notebook chrome and an inbox make agent contributions legible and controllable.

impact_evidence: Combines observer place/time, visibility, object types, and comfortable route.

usability_note: Progressive preview and approval should make complex astronomy planning approachable.

one_line: Agent-native paid API discovery and purchase preparation with wallet-enforced payment boundaries.
what_it_does: Lets agents search paid APIs, inspect machine schemas, and prepare x402 payment challenges without signing or paying; wallet tooling retains authority.
leverage_rationale: Structured catalog, schema, price, and 402 challenge tools make precise micro-purchase preparation reliable while preventing conversational authority from crossing into payment.
leverage_evidence: Three tools expose search_paid_resources, get_resource_schema, and prepare_purchase.
Outputs include price, currency, query contract, repurchase policy, and exact payment accepts.

execution_evidence: Public repository, alive demo, and three frame sheets are reported.

impact_evidence: Targets recurring agent jobs and delta-only change feeds.

standouts: Clearest payment safety boundary: discovery can inform but cannot authorize spending.
advance_reason: Strong agent infrastructure value, safety design, and evidence of a real product integration.
